newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Cimpor Brazilian deal worth 62 bln esc.
newsitem.headline: Cimpor Brazilian deal worth 62 bln esc.

text.p: Portuguese cement producer Cimpor-Cimentos de Portugal said in a statement it had acquired two Brazilian cement businesses for 62 billion escudos ($394 million).
It said it had acquired CISAFRA, a cement producer, and the SERRANA group's cement business.
The two acquisitions represent total cement assets, including shareholders' equity, financial debt and investments in progress, of $177 per tonne of production capacity.
Cimpor said that the production capacity of the acquired facilities would reach about three million tons per year.

It said Cimpor's cement production capacity in Portugal, Spain, Mozambique, Morocco and Brazil would stand at 11 million tonnes per year and total sales would be nine million tons per year after the latest acquisitions.
In the medium term Brazil is expected to represent 14 percent of Cimpor's turnover and 16 percent of its operating income, the company said.
Cimpor said it had purchased, directly and indirectly, shares representing 67.3 percent of CISAFRA's capital and 99.97 percent of its voting rights.

A new company will be created for SERRANA's cement business, it said. Cimpor has signed a contract under which it guarantees the acquisition of shares representing 76.6 percent of the new company's capital.

According to the deal made with the seller, the Bunge Group, Cimpor assumes an obligation to launch a bid over the remaining shares. This will happen as soon as the necessary legal requirements can be fulfilled.
CISAFRA owns a cement plant in the state of Bahia and distribution terminals in several regions where it operates.
The company is focused on the northeastern market, where its commercial activities target the Bahia and Piaui states, holding market shares of 13 percent and 15 percent respectively.
CISAFRA is also active, although not with such strong market positions, in the states of Pernambuco and Ceara, Cimpor said.
SERRANA's cement business includes two cement plants, one in the state of Sao Paulo and another in the state of Rio Grande do Sul where it also owns a milling facility.
In its home market in the south and southeast of Brazil, SERRANA holds a market share of six percent. In Rio Grande do Sul its market share reaches 32 percent.

Cimpor said that after the acquisitions it would be operating in the northeast, southeast and south of Brazil with a market share of five percent, a significant position in the Brazilian cement industry.
"With this investment, Cimpor pursues its internationalisation strategy, as previously presented to its shareholders," the company said.
"The company is diversifying the geographic area of its operations through acquisitions outside Portugal and Galicia in high growth markets with different economic cycles," it added.
